paragraphs.text: It's about 278 kilometres across at its longest.
Start with the assumption. The first obstacle is knowing what it is made of; hauling metal across the Solar System comes after.
That is the first effect — but not the biggest. Assume humans tried to mine the metal-rich asteroid Psyche.

The second-order effect is stranger. Psyche is the only core-like metal world we know. It's about 278 kilometres across at its longest. Its density is around 4 grams per cubic centimetre. Pure iron-nickel would be nearly double that, at 7.9. So Psyche is likely metal mixed with rock or rubble. NASA's probe launched in 2023 and should arrive in 2029. Mining it would mean hauling metal across hundreds of millions of kilometres. So first we have to learn what it's actually made of. Psyche has a shape consistent with a Jacobi ellipsoid and dimensions within a few km of 278 km x 238 km x 171 km. Psyche has a bulk density of 3.977±0.253 g/cm3, considerably higher than most small Solar System bodies. The iron-nickel found in most iron meteorites has a bulk density of 7.9 g/cm3. The Psyche spacecraft was launched on 13 October 2023, with an expected arrival in 2029. 16 Psyche is the only metallic core-like body discovered so far. A body's bulk density reveals its mix of metal, rock and empty space before anyone lands on it. Humans tried to mine the metal-rich asteroid Psyche.
And here is where science stops being certain. The governing physics: a body's bulk density reveals its mix of metal, rock and empty space before anyone lands on it.
So what is the answer? The exact timeline depends on how the impossible change happens; the order of effects is what established physics constrains.

miniNarrative: Assume humans tried to mine the metal-rich asteroid Psyche.
Despite their large numbers, asteroids are a relatively recent discovery, with the first one—Ceres—only being identified in 1801.
Only one asteroid, 4 Vesta, which has a relatively reflective surface, is normally visible to the naked eye in dark skies when it is favorably positioned.
Rarely, small asteroids passing close to Earth may be briefly visible to the naked eye.
shorts.payoff: As of May 2025, the Minor Planet Center had data on 1,460,356 minor planets in the inner and outer Solar System, of which about 826,864 had enough information to be given numbered designations.
